title: Domain-Specific LLM Fine-Tuning Pipeline with QLoRA, Token Packing & Automated Evaluation
problem: General-purpose language models perform unreliably on specialized domain tasks involving legal statute interpretation, clinical terminology, and proprietary API code generation. Full parameter fine-tuning is computationally prohibitive, requiring multi-node GPU clusters and millions of dollars. This project builds a parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) pipeline in Python and PyTorch. The system ingests structured domain corpora, quantizes base open-source transformer models to 4-bit precision via bitsandbytes, injects Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) matrices into attention and feed-forward layers, trains models with sequence packing and gradient checkpointing, tracks loss curves in Weights & Biases, and evaluates domain accuracy improvements against base zero-shot models.

use_cases.title: Clinical Terminology and Pathology Report Extraction
use_cases.first_sentence: Healthcare research institutions require language models that extract structured disease codes and laboratory findings from unstructured pathology text.
use_cases.second_sentence: The pipeline fine-tunes a base 7B parameter open-source model on clinical datasets, increasing biomedical entity extraction accuracy without exposing training data to third-party APIs.

use_cases.title: Corporate Regulatory Compliance & Statutory Q&A
use_cases.first_sentence: Corporate legal teams need specialized models capable of answering queries regarding cross-jurisdictional data privacy regulations and corporate bylaws.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine trains LoRA adapters on statutory corpora, enabling localized legal question answering with precise section citations and low hallucination rates.

use_cases.title: Internal Proprietary Software Framework Code Generation
use_cases.first_sentence: Software engineering organizations with proprietary internal SDKs and private libraries require code assistance tools tailored to their non-public APIs.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system fine-tunes base coding models on internal repository functions, generating syntactically valid code completions that respect internal abstractions.

hard_parts: Configuring 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization and double quantization to fit 7B parameter models within consumer GPU VRAM limits
Implementing sequence packing algorithms that concatenate short training samples to maximize compute utilization without cross-sample attention leakage
Selecting optimal LoRA rank (r) and alpha hyperparameters across attention projections to prevent catastrophic forgetting
Benchmarking fine-tuned adapter weights against zero-shot base baselines to verify genuine domain generalization
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase separating dataset tokenization scripts, LoRA configuration modules, and evaluation harnesses
Reproducible training pipeline with public Weights & Biases run logs demonstrating smooth loss convergence and gradient norm stability
Anti-fake verification script loading merged LoRA adapter weights and verifying domain-specific terminology generation on unseen prompts

architecture.data_flow: Domain instruction datasets enter the tokenization engine; sequences pack into dense context blocks with appropriate masking; the base model loads in 4-bit precision using bitsandbytes; LoRA adapter matrices inject into target query, key, value, and projection layers; PyTorch executes mixed-precision training steps with AdamW optimizer and cosine learning rate schedules; training metrics stream to Weights & Biases; upon completion, adapter weights merge into the base checkpoint; the evaluation harness scores generation accuracy across held-out domain test sets.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Gradient clipping at 1.0 preventing exploding gradients; sequence length truncation preventing out-of-memory GPU crashes.

targets.report: Domain evaluation accuracy comparison report and benchmark score table

targets.target: Peak VRAM allocation during training step is < 8.5 gigabytes
targets.report: GPU memory allocation profile and VRAM benchmark trace

targets.minimum_pass: Training throughput is >= 650 tokens per second
targets.target: Training throughput is >= 1,450 tokens per second
targets.report: Training execution timing log and token throughput summary

environment.gpu: 12GB+ VRAM GPU recommended (Google Colab T4 / Kaggle free GPU tier / local NVIDIA GPU)
environment.cost: $0 (fully executable on free Google Colab / Kaggle GPU tiers or local hardware)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: Free HuggingFace account for base model downloads and free Weights & Biases account
environment.reference_environment: Ubuntu 22.04 with NVIDIA GPU (12GB+ VRAM), PyTorch 2.1+, CUDA 12.1, and HuggingFace transformers
environment.fallback_path: CPU training with TinyLlama (1.1B) using bitsandbytes CPU quantization or mock forward-pass runner

riskiest_component.name: GPU Out-of-Memory (OOM) Errors During Attention Backward Passes
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enable gradient checkpointing, FlashAttention-2, and per-device batch size of 1 with gradient accumulation.
riskiest_component.fallback: Reduce sequence length to 512 tokens and use LoRA rank r=8 instead of r=16.
